evidence: Plaut. As. 1.3.26: piscis nēquam est, nisi recēns (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not long made or gathered: fresh fish, bread, milk. Its opposite is vetus; novus is new rather than fresh.

phrases.latin: Tantummodo sī passer recēns est vēnālis hodiē.
phrases.english: Only if fresh flounder is for sale today.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 69, 71; p. 318.
